What Zelda analyzed The work behind this report — counted, not estimated. 12 Pages analyzed 12 Sections searched 2 Categories analyzed Business Model & Growth Analysis Insufficient disclosed data to describe the business model. No revenue model, pricing structure, customer acquisition approach, or expansion strategy was extracted from the document. The only evidence of commercial activity is the self-reported traction data: the company states 140,000+ bots [S1] and 500M messages (with an ambiguity in measurement basis between a cumulative total and a monthly rate [S2, S3]) in a slide context headed 'Traction by Apr-16'. Whether these metrics reflect paying customers, free users, or a mix is not stated. Who pays — businesses, developers, or end users — is not found in the extracted evidence. What drives growth and any stated expansion plans are similarly absent. Information Readiness Score: 12/100 Present: • Self-reported traction metrics: 140,000+ bots [S1] and 500M messages [S2] within a 'Traction by Apr-16' slide context • Self-reported message volume rate: 500M messages/month [S3] • Narrated funding figure: $23.1M raised, as listed by Pitch Deck Hunt [S4] • Company stage (Series A) and sector (Software) from profile [P1, P2] Needs Validation: • Funding raised figure — no external evidence found [C1] • Usage metrics — no external evidence found [C2, C3, C4] • Clarification of whether 500M messages is a cumulative total or a monthly rate [C2, C3] • Revenue, burn rate, use of proceeds, and cash position — not found in extracted evidence • Team identities and credentials — not found in extracted evidence • Product description and differentiation — not found in extracted evidence • Problem statement and customer definition — not found in extracted evidence • Market size — not found in extracted evidence • Risk factors — not found in extracted evidence Next evidence to supply: Audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements showing revenue, gross margin, and burn rate as of a stated date, alongside a clear definition of the 500M messages metric (cumulative or monthly) with supporting platform data. Supported Points • Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M raised for ManyChat [S4], providing at least a narrated indication of funding history, though the figure lacks a stated date and has not been independently verified [C1]. • The company states that 140,000+ bots had been created and 500M messages delivered, presented in a slide context headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2], indicating the platform had reached non-trivial scale in bot deployment by that reference point, if the self-reported figures are accurate. Open Concerns • The 500M messages metric is presented with two different measurement bases across the deck — without a stated time interval on page 10 and as 500M/month on page 12 [C2, C3] — and this inconsistency has not been resolved; it is unknown whether the figures represent the same event measured differently or distinct data points, which directly affects interpretation of platform scale. • Revenue is entirely absent from the extracted evidence, leaving unknown whether the bot and message volumes translate into any paying customer base or commercial traction. • No team information was extracted, meaning the identities, domain expertise, and track records of the founders are unknown — a material gap for assessing execution risk at Series A. • No product description, competitive positioning, or differentiation was extracted, leaving it unknown how ManyChat's platform differs from alternatives and why customers would continue to use it. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece of evidence is a dated revenue and customer breakdown — specifically, the number of paying customers, average revenue per user, and monthly recurring revenue as of a stated date — which would determine whether ManyChat's self-reported usage metrics [S1, S2, S3] correspond to a real commercial business or an unmonetised user base.
